subject: Request: one-time incentive for Nimbus Health — hybrid routing rollout delay
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-06-20T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Request: one-time incentive for Nimbus Health — hybrid routing rollout delay

Team,

Quick summary: Nimbus Health is live on Redwood (hosted) and was depending on our hybrid-routing feature to reduce egress/transfer costs and guarantee our promised 99th %-tile latency for multi-region failover. The hybrid routing rollout we planned for June was delayed by two weeks due to a kernel compatibility issue; Nimbus saw higher-than-expected token costs and a short spike in p99 for some sustained workloads. They reached out asking for a commercial gesture while the feature lands.

Customer impact numbers (Q2 week window) attached — see nimbus_impact_q2.xlsx. Key points: ~35% higher token spend vs. forecast (~$28k incremental in the month), and two incidents where p99 crossed the SLO for 6–10 minutes each.

Asks from Nimbus: 1) one-time credit to offset the incremental spend, or 2) a temporary reduced per-token rate for 3 months, or 3) a short Dedicated burst at no charge for two weeks while they finish smoke tests.

Options I propose for consideration (quick, not final):
- Option A (preferred): One-time credit equal to the documented excess spend for June (~$28k) plus a goodwill credit of $5k.
- Option B: Temporary 20% per-token discount for 3 months (capped at $40k).
- Option C: Two-week Dedicated burst (N1 equivalent) + $10k credit.

We need an accelerated approval here — Nimbus is negotiating renewal timing with procurement next week. Can Product confirm the ETA and that the rollout will include rollback/fallback safeguards? Finance/legal — please advise cap and phrasing so we don't create an open-ended precedent. Vanessa/CS — can you validate the customer's ask and whether the goodwill credit is sufficient to preserve the renewal?

Attachments: nimbus_impact_q2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-22T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: one-time incentive for Nimbus Health — hybrid routing rollout delay

Thanks Marcus — reviewed the impact spreadsheet. A few clarifying points before I recommend any engineering commitment: 

- The kernel compatibility fix is merged; scheduled rollout for the remaining customers is 2027-06-28 with a staged canary across two regions. We expect the p99 risk window to be closed after that, but I want to confirm rollback behavior if we detect regressions.
- The telemetry indicates the spike was correlated with a particular multi-model ensemble path they use. We can add a targeted KV-cache warm path for that route; it requires a config change and 1 day of ops time.

From a product standpoint I can commit to the rollout timeline (June 28–30) and the targeted config work if we get sign-off to prioritize it for Nimbus this week. That reduces the ongoing risk; I'd prefer Option C (Dedicated burst) for the short horizon while we validate, plus a modest credit to cover the spike — it keeps us within operational controls.

I'm looping in Vanessa for customer surface-level confirmation, and Karthik for finance implications.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-24T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: one-time incentive for Nimbus Health — hybrid routing rollout delay

Marcus / Laura —

Thanks for the write-up and the numbers. I ran a quick model with finance and legal; here's what we should consider for approval paths and guardrails: 

1) Approver: Anything <= $25k credit can be approved by Sales Director + Finance. Anything > $25k requires VP/Exec sign-off (Evelyn).
2) Structure recommendation: Approve Option C but replace the uncapped goodwill credit with a firm one-time credit of $15k and the two-week Dedicated burst. Rationale: preserves renewal economics, limited downside exposure.
3) Contract language: we should call this a "one-time service credit" tied to the hybrid-routing rollout delay; explicitly exclude ongoing discounts to avoid precedent. Legal will draft an amendment.
4) Accounting: if we issue the Dedicated burst as a service-credit, we need to record usage offsets; finance will require updated forecast impact to the quarter.

I've attached approval_matrix.pdf that maps approvers and required artifacts. If Sales wants a larger commercial (Option A sized at ~$33k) we need an exec note approving a customer retention exception; that would be escalated.

Recommended next step: Marcus, confirm Nimbus prefers the Dedicated burst + $15k credit option (Option C-mod). If yes, I'll prepare the email for Evelyn with the approval matrix and the forecast delta for sign-off.

-Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: approval_matrix.pdf

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Billing <billing@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: one-time incentive for Nimbus Health — hybrid routing rollout delay

Team —

Appreciate the clear options and the fast follow from Product and RevOps. I reviewed the numbers and the approval matrix. Executive decision: approve Option C-mod as recommended by Karthik — two-week Dedicated burst and a one-time service credit of $15,000. Conditions: 

1) This is a one-time customer retention credit tied explicitly to DL-2027-0451; language will be added to the renewal amendment that this is not precedent for future feature delays.
2) Product (Laura) to confirm the rollout schedule and provide a short post-deployment report (48h) documenting that p99 returned to SLO and KV-cache mitigations were applied.
3) Billing to record the credit and Dedicated burst as a contra-revenue adjustment for Q2; Finance to include the forecast delta in the July revenue brief.

Vanessa — please notify Nimbus (Aisha) and coordinate the Dedicated burst window (targeting July 5–19) and the amendment signature. Marcus — please send the external-facing note and loop procurement. Karthik — please finalize the approval doc and hand off to Billing/Legal for formal amendment.

Thanks everyone for the quick turn. I want this to be narrow and time-boxed — get the customer through renewal and ensure Product fixes are validated.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
